newsitem.title: FRANCE: French utilities, unions sign for shorter week.
newsitem.headline: French utilities, unions sign for shorter week.

text.p: France's state electricity and gas utilities signed an agreement with three trade unions on Friday which will allow staff to cut their working week to 32 hours from 38, paid for 35 hours.

It said the three year-deal, signed by the CFDT, CFTC and CGC unions, would allow it to maintain staff levels, currently at 142,000 and that it would otherwise only have been able to recruit 5,000-7,000 over the three years to replace 11,000 parting with early retirement packages.

The signature of three unions is enough to implement the plan, which allows for voluntary acceptance of the shorter work week but also allows for many of those recruited in the future to be taken on for a 32 hour week.

The deal, open for renewal in three years, does not have the backing of the Force Ouvriere union and the Communist-led CGT union has vowed to mobilise its staff against the agreement, which requires union backing at the level of 200 EdF and GdF plant level for many of the other provisions.
The utilities said that, beyond the agreement to maintain staff levels, their agreement set an objective for the longer term of hiring 15,000 staff, mainly younger workers.
For managers who worked 50 hours a week on average, the utilities said a four-day week or extended holidays would be used rather than a defined shorter working period.
One of the other facets of the deal is greater flexibility in opening and work hours to include Saturdays and during the normal work week to extend the stretch of the day to 0500 GMT to 2000 GMT.
